svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: Event-driven order processing on AWS subtitle: One Amazon EventBridge bus fans order events out to an AWS Step Functions workflow, an Amazon SQS billing queue and an Amazon SNS topic direction: down # merge: false gives the dashed fan-outs from the bus and from the SNS topic their own ports # instead of one shared trunk each. layout: { merge: false } legend: solid: Order path dashed: Other rule targets and subscribers groups: cloud: { type: aws:cloud } region: { type: aws:region, label: us-east-1, in: cloud } workflow: { type: aws:step-functions, label: AWS Step Functions workflow, in: region } nodes: customers: { icon: aws:users, label: Customers } api: { icon: aws:api-gateway, label: Amazon API Gateway, note: POST /orders, in: region } bus: { icon: aws:eventbridge-custom-event-bus, label: Orders event bus, note: Amazon EventBridge, in: region, align: api } reserve: { icon: aws:lambda, label: AWS Lambda, note: Reserve stock, in: workflow } charge: { icon: aws:lambda, label: AWS Lambda, note: Charge payment, in: workflow } ship: { icon: aws:lambda, label: AWS Lambda, note: Create shipment, in: workflow } table: { icon: aws:dynamodb-table, label: Orders table, note: Amazon DynamoDB, in: region } billing: { icon: aws:simple-queue-service-queue, label: Billing queue, note: Amazon SQS queue, in: region } invoice: { icon: aws:lambda, label: AWS Lambda, note: Invoice generator, in: region } notices: { icon: aws:simple-notification-service-topic, label: Order notifications, note: Amazon SNS topic, in: region } email: { icon: aws:simple-notification-service-email-notification, label: Email subscription, in: region } analytics: { icon: aws:simple-queue-service-queue, label: Analytics queue, note: Amazon SQS queue, in: region } edges: # The solid path is the main story. EventBridge invokes every target asynchronously, so # dashed marks the other rule targets and subscribers, not a different delivery mode. - customers -> api: HTTPS - api -> bus: { label: OrderPlaced } - bus -> workflow: { label: fulfillment rule } # constraint: false keeps the three workflow steps side by side in one row instead of three rows. - { from: reserve, to: charge, constraint: false } - { from: charge, to: ship, constraint: false } - workflow -> table: { label: order status } - bus --> billing: billing rule - billing --> invoice - bus --> notices: notification rule - notices --> email, analytics

svg.title: Event-driven order processing on AWS
svg.desc: Event-driven order processing on AWS. 12 components in 3 groups. Connections: Customers to Amazon API Gateway (HTTPS); Amazon API Gateway to Orders event bus (OrderPlaced); Orders event bus to AWS Step Functions workflow (fulfillment rule); AWS Lambda to AWS Lambda; AWS Lambda to AWS Lambda; AWS Step Functions workflow to Orders table (order status); Orders event bus to Billing queue (billing rule); Billing queue to AWS Lambda; Orders event bus to Order notifications (notification rule); Order notifications to Email subscription; Order notifications to Analytics queue.

text.tspan: One Amazon EventBridge bus fans order events out to an AWS Step Functions workflow, an Amazon SQS billing queue and an Amazon SNS topic
